answer: The anti-Sybil mechanism is a per-identity registration bond with slashing. Each agent identity must lock real capital on-chain, forfeited if it is caught colluding, so reputation cannot be farmed hollow with free duplicates: every extra puppet carries the same up-front lock. Sybil attacks pay only when many identities cost less than one, and the bond erases that discount. A sudden gale of parallel votes means capital locked rather than nothing spent. Cost scales with identity count while payout is fixed, so at the vertex the attacker's margin turns negative and the swarm stops paying.
